mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Yield curve inverts (10y-2y < 0) within the next 6 months, or GDP growth accelerates but SPX returns are negative over the next 60 trading days in >50% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate, defined as a 0.5 percentage point rise over the past 3 months, signals a rapidly weakening labor market that will pressure consumer spending and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Unemployment rate rises sharply but consumer confidence (Conference Board index) also rises over the next month, or SPX returns are positive in >60% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production growth (year-over-year percent change) exceeds 4% for two consecutive months, it signals strong demand that will boost corporate revenues and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO YoY growth > 4% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: Industrial production growth remains strong but ISM Manufacturing PMI falls below 45 within the next 3 months, or SPX returns are negative in >40% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is above 4% and rising, it signals a tightening monetary policy that will pressure equity valuations and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Federal funds rate rises above 4% but 2-year Treasury yield falls below 3% within the next 3 months, or SPX returns are positive in >50% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts growth (year-over-year percent change) exceeds 20% for two consecutive months, it signals a strong housing market that will boost consumer spending and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST YoY growth > 20% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: Housing starts growth remains strong but existing home sales (NAR series) fall year-over-year for two consecutive months, or SPX returns are negative in >40% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 4% and payroll employment growth (3-month moving average) exceeds 200,000 jobs per month, it signals a tight labor market that will boost wage growth and consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Labor market remains tight but average hourly earnings growth (BLS series) falls below 2% year-over-year, or SPX returns are negative in >50% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPI) growth (year-over-year percent change) exceeds 3% for three consecutive months, it signals rising inflationary pressures that will pressure real earnings and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL YoY growth > 3% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: CPI growth remains elevated but the 10-year breakeven inflation rate (TIPS spread) falls below 2%, or SPX returns are positive in >60% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (PCE) growth (year-over-year percent change) falls below 2% for two consecutive quarters, it signals a weakening consumer sector that will pressure corporate revenues and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS YoY growth < 2% for 2 consecutive quarters
failure_condition: Real PCE growth remains weak but the University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment Index rises by more than 5 points over the next 3 months, or SPX returns are positive in >50% of triggered instances.
